messages:
mira: heads-up: escalated customer (ACME corp) is hitting repeated SSE reconnects from our Go SDK. They report partial responses after a reconnect and memory growth in their service. sending logs in thread. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-3421 :warning:

jack: saw the ticket. can you paste a minimal repro + the exact sdk version?

mira: SDK: go-redwood v0.9.7 (we bumped from v0.9.5 last week). repro steps (from customer):
1) establish streaming chat via Go SDK iterator (using default backoff)
2) upstream endpoint returns 503 + Retry-After for ~30s (simulated)
3) client reconnects automatically (sdk resumes)
4) subsequent chunks are interleaved/duplicated or client sees truncated JSON in some events
5) memory (RSS) in their service climbs after ~100 reconnects

kevin: can you paste the iterator usage pattern? (maybe they're not draining/closing)

mira: here's the snippet they provided:```go
ctx := context.Background()
iter, err := client.StreamChat(ctx, req)
if err != nil {
  return err
}
for iter.Next() {
  tok := iter.Event()
  // process token -> append to buffer
}
if err := iter.Err(); err != nil {
  return err
}
// they don't always call iter.Close() because they rely on Next() returning false on EOF
```

ingrid: that looks plausible. I remember a change in v0.9.7 where we changed reconnection to attempt "resume" semantics instead of full restart to preserve server-side deltas. If resume logic reuses the previous decoder instance it could leak state.

jack: do we have logs showing partial JSON?

mira: customer log snippet (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-05T15:22:11Z] INFO reconnecting after 503, retry-after=30
[2026-03-05T15:22:41Z] INFO resumed stream, last_event_id=ev_1291
[2026-03-05T15:22:41Z] ERROR json decode failed: unexpected EOF
[2026-03-05T15:22:41Z] INFO received chunk: "{\"delta\":\"Here is the fi"
[2026-03-05T15:22:41Z] INFO received chunk: "nal part.\"}\n{\"delta\":\"Another message"
[2026-03-05T15:22:41Z] INFO downstream processed buffer: "{\"delta\":\"Here is the final part.\"}\n{\"delta\":\"Another message\""
```
They then show that 2nd object is not terminated and later gets combined with next reconnect's fragments, causing duplication when replays occur.

kevin: so two problems: 1) decoder state/fragment buffer is carried across reconnects 2) reconnect attempts keep spawning goroutines that hold onto buffers if Close() isn't called. Could explain RSS growth.

mira: customer also raised billing concern: duplicates ended up being recharged because they count tokens for partial fragments re-sent during resume. they want a mitigation asap.

jack: can we reproduce locally? I'll simulate server that returns 503 and then resumes with fragments.

deploy-bot: deployment reminder: there was a streaming reconnect change merged in PR #1043 on 2026-02-28 to add resume semantics (author: ingrid).

ingrid: yes that was my PR. It introduced a resume path that attempts to resume from last_event_id and preserves an internal chunk buffer across connections to stitch truncated frames. I see now how that could keep references alive if Next() isn't called to drain. We assumed iter.Next() lifecycle would always be well-formed.

jack: quick local repro steps I ran:
- run tiny server that returns 503 then a resumed SSE stream with deliberate half-chunks
- run example Go client (same iterator pattern)
- after ~50 reconnects, rss increases by ~18MB and goroutine count grows
- observed leftover goroutines waiting in line to read from a closed connection

kevin: checkbox: confirm whether iter.Close() cancels background goroutine. If not, that's a bug.

mira: customer says they rely on library auto-reconnect and rarely call Close() (they rely on Next() to finish). we should make Close() optional: SDK must not leak if user code doesn't call Close() in typical loops.

ingrid: agreed. Plan from my side: revert the resume buffer being held globally; instead create a short-lived stitcher that lives only for the new connection and never holds onto previous connection resources. Also make sure iterator has finalizer/Cleanup when context is cancelled.

jack: actionable repro I pushed to my sandbox repo: https://git.internal/redwood/sse-repro (branch: jack/sse-leak-repro). includes small server + client and a script to run 200 reconnects.

mira: customer-run logs show also a sequence where server returned 503 with `Retry-After: 0` (immediate) which made the client spin-reconnect faster than expected. Their traffic multiplied and they saw token duplication spikes in billing for a short window.

kevin: we should throttle reconnect attempts and ensure exponential backoff respects Retry-After header. Also dedupe token counting on the server side if event IDs are replayed within a small window. I'll open a backend ticket.

ingrid: immediate SDK patch I propose:
- ensure NewIterator spawns a background reader bound to the current connection only; on reconnect, cancel and wait for background reader to exit before creating a new one (prevent leaks)
- do not reuse in-memory JSON buffer across connections; use a new buffer per connection and merge safely only for currently-active connection fragments
- make iterator.Close() idempotent and also tie it to ctx cancellation (if ctx.Done() then Close())
- add debug telemetry: reconnect_count, last_event_id, outstanding_buffers

jack: timeline? can we patch a hotfix release 0.9.8-rc1 with minimal changes (no API surface change) and ask customer to test?

ingrid: yes I can cut a patch and include unit tests + the sandbox repro. I'll add a runtime safeguard that if reconnect_count > 10 within 10m we log a WARN and stop auto-resume (fail the stream) to avoid billing storms. That preserves safety.

mira: customer wants workaround if we can't get them a patch immediately. Suggested workaround: force their code to call iter.Close() on errors and add a guard to recreate client for each stream (not ideal). Could also throttle at their LB. I'll pass both options.

kevin: I opened backend ticket BILL-987 to investigate dedup protection and short window credits. tagging infra/billing.

qa-bot: automated note: added flaky test coverage for SSE reconnect scenarios -> tests/sse_reconnect_test.go (CI job: sse-reconnect, expected flakiness false).

jack: next steps:
- ingrid to open PR with fix + tests (ETA 24h)
- jack to run repro in prod-like environment and confirm memory/goroutine leak fixed (ETA 48h)
- kevin to coordinate billing dedupe investigation and alert customer (ETA 48-72h)
- mira to relay temporary workaround and request logs from customer when they can perform test
ingrid: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/1102 (draft). patch summary in PR: "ensure per-connection stitcher, tie reader lifecycle to connection context, idempotent Close()". added unit tests for partial chunk stitching and for goroutine cleanup.

mira: customer replied: "thanks — we'll try rc tomorrow and will keep an eye on token counts" :thumbsup:

jack: I'll run load test tonight. if all green we can push 0.9.8 release. Also add a short doc blurb in changelog about resume behavior and that resume is disabled after too many reconnects to avoid duplicate billing.

ingrid: will add telemetry metrics so we can alert when resume storms happen. also adding a small note in SDK README about best practices: call Close() when possible and prefer one iterator per request.

kevin: good. set follow-up on Monday to close the billing ticket or escalate to finance if duplicates can't be refunded automatically.

mira: thanks team — will update ticket CS-3421 with links to PR and repro and let customer know next steps. :white_check_mark:
